functions.funcDef: Generate and control thrust for all phases of flight, including continued flight after loss of one engine.
functions.subDef: Inputs: thrust/reverse commands from flight deck (AVI), fuel at engine inlet (FUE). Processing: FADEC dual-channel control of four turbofans (PRP). Outputs: thrust; reverse thrust on inboard engines; engine parameter data to AVI. Independence: single-engine loss alone does not defeat continued flight ("continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine").

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic control surfaces to provide control authority across the flight envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.
functions.subName: Position primary and secondary flight control surfaces
functions.subDef: Inputs: pilot inceptor position and autopilot commands, air/inertial data (AVI), hydraulic power (HYD A/B/C), electrical power (EPS). Processing: three dissimilar flight control computers voting (FCS). Outputs: surface position, envelope-protection and jam/asymmetry status to AVI. Independence: dual actuation per surface from different hydraulic systems; mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and lower rudder.

functions.funcName: Support the aircraft on the ground and decelerate on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support landing and taxi loads on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces and provide braking and ground directional control within the landing distance requirement.
functions.subName: Provide wheel braking and ground steering
functions.subDef: Inputs: crew commands from pedals/tiller/gear lever, weight-on-wheels and wheel speed (AVI), hydraulic power (HYD A/B). Processing: electrically signalled, hydraulically actuated carbon multi-disc braking with anti-skid per wheel pair; hydraulic nose-wheel steering (LDG). Outputs: braking force, steering, brake temperature/tyre pressure to AVI. Independence: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve sized to six brake applications; free-fall extension independent of hydraulic pressure.

functions.funcDef: Position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the hold length and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases.
functions.subDef: Inputs: electrical power (EPS), loading plan/weight-and-balance from ground system, weight-on-wheels (LDG), nose door position (NZD). Processing: nine saddles with two tensioned straps each and a single instrumented tension monitoring loop (CRG). Outputs: strap tension and saddle engagement to flight deck; payload mass/distribution to CG computation; restraint status to take-off configuration monitor. Independence: loss of any one strap carried by neighbours; single monitoring loop is a recorded coverage item.

functions.funcName: Provide payload access and pressure boundary at the nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in hold access via the upward-hinging nose visor and maintain the forward pressure boundary when closed.
functions.subName: Lock and confirm the nose door closed
functions.subDef: Inputs: hydraulic power (HYD A and lock-actuator supply), electrical backup power (EPS), pressurisation state (ECS), crew/ground command. Processing: twelve rotary latches and eight locking pins with a pressure interlock; dual dissimilar lock sensing (NZD). Outputs: lock status to flight deck and take-off configuration monitor; pressure boundary integrity to ECS. Independence: two hydraulic supplies, electric backup, two dissimilar independently-routed sensing paths; door structure itself is not a function (treated as structure).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the pressure differential across the fuselage.
functions.subDef: Inputs: bleed air (PRP/APU), ram air, electrical power (EPS), flight deck selections, weight-on-wheels and door position. Processing: two digital controllers driving two outflow valves with a pneumatic backup (ECS). Outputs: conditioned air; differential pressure/cabin altitude to AVI and crew oxygen logic; pressure state to nose door interlock. Independence: two controllers, two outflow valves, pneumatic backup, and independent mechanical relief valves.

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes within the icing envelope of the certification basis.
functions.subName: Heat protected surfaces, inlets and probes
functions.subDef: Inputs: bleed air from the cross-bleed manifold, AC/DC electrical power (EPS), total air temperature and airspeed (AVI), crew selection. Processing: bleed-air protection to wing leading edges and cowls, six electrically heated stabiliser zones, electrically heated probes/ports/windshields and two ice detectors (IPS). Outputs: ice protection status/zone health and detection advisory to AVI. Independence: bleed available from either side via cross-bleed manifold; independently supplied electrical zones; two ice detectors of identical type recorded as a commonality item.

functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host prioritised alerting.
functions.subName: Present displays and consolidated crew alerts
functions.subDef: Inputs: data from every aircraft system, electrical power from main and essential buses, pitot/static/AoA sensing, navigation signals. Processing: three display processors on dual deterministic networks, three air data inertial reference units, two-channel alerting, independent standby instrument (AVI). Outputs: displays and prioritised alerts to crew; commands to autopilot/autothrottle; recorded parameters to FDR. Independence: standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric thrust producing uncommanded yawing moment (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded yawing/rolling moment; worst case an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm — the stated directional-control sizing case. Requires rudder authority and possibly asymmetric-power management to hold heading/track.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect yaw via displays/handling and apply rudder and thrust adjustment; workload elevated, particularly at low speed near V1.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects support a MAJOR-to-HAZARDOUS range depending on when the asymmetry occurs (low-speed/high-workout near V1 vs cruise) and the resulting margin against the sized rudder authority — the SDD states this is the directional-control sizing case but does not quantify residual controllability. Left blank pending the controllability margin and worst-phase determination; do not average across phases.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to crew command (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Commanded thrust not achieved as intended (e.g. more/less/wrong direction of thrust change), producing an unexpected trajectory or speed excursion; if it manifests asymmetrically it also imposes a yawing moment.
fha.effCrew: Crew observe mismatch between commanded and achieved thrust on displays and handling; intervene by re-commanding, switching autothrottle off, or managing engines manually; workload elevated.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The function definition ('control thrust magnitude and direction') supports stating a trajectory/speed effect, but the AMOUNT and DIRECTION of the erroneous response, the phase in which it is worst, and whether it presents symmetrically or asymmetrically are not grounded in the provided material. Cannot derive a defensible class from the effects as stated; left blank pending characterisation of the error magnitude and worst phase.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Gradual undetected thrust asymmetry below crew detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Slowly developing thrust asymmetry not annunciated and below the crew handling-cue threshold; produces a persistent uncommanded yaw/roll trimmed out by the crew or autopilot without recognition of the underlying asymmetry, degrading margin against the sized rudder authority and masking a developing condition.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action regarding it (unaware case); autopilot/trim may absorb the asymmetry, hiding it until margin is consumed or a further failure occurs.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — An undetected condition that erodes directional-control margin can be more severe than the detected case because no crew mitigation is credited and it can combine with a subsequent event. Whether the accumulated asymmetry threatens continued safe flight depends on the detection threshold and the residual rudder margin — neither is given. Left blank pending detection-threshold and controllability-margin data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous thrust command (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Thrust delivered differs from that intended without annunciation or evident handling cue; aircraft follows an unintended speed/trajectory not recognised by the crew, with no mitigation credited until the divergence becomes apparent.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue duties normally and take no action (unaware case); the error is not annunciated, so recovery is delayed until the effect becomes perceptible through raw handling/energy state.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be derived: the magnitude and direction of the erroneous, undetected command and its worst-phase consequence are not grounded in the provided material, and no crew mitigation is credited in the unaware case. A trajectory/energy effect can be stated but not classified without the error magnitude and worst-phase outcome. Left blank per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of available thrust (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust available; bounded case is loss of one engine, which the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after at/after V1, with degraded climb performance. Loss of a second engine on the same side is outside the design dispatch case and remains to be studied, and may not be bounded by the single-engine case.
fha.effCrew: Crew manage the reduced-thrust condition per procedure — identify the affected engine, secure it (fuel shut-off, fire handle), and continue to a suitable aerodrome; workload elevated, more so at low speed near V1.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — 'Partial loss' spans from a single-engine loss (design-continuation case, plausibly MAJOR) to multiple/same-side loss the SDD explicitly holds open as 'a condition to be studied' — so the worst case within this partial-loss condition is not bounded by the material. Classifying per §25.1309 on the worst applicable phase requires the second-engine and same-side effects to be resolved. Left blank pending that study; do not classify to the benign single-engine case alone.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of thrust from one propulsive source causing controllable asymmetry
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust from one engine produces a yawing/rolling moment requiring rudder input to maintain directional control; reduced total thrust and climb performance. Outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the directional-control sizing case.
fha.effCrew: Increased workload to counter yaw, retrim, and manage the engine-out drill; continued flight to a suitable aerodrome is available per the design intent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine-out is within the design dispatch case (continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at/after V1) and is controllable; effects are a significant reduction in performance/safety margin and increased crew workload, consistent with Major. Engineer to confirm against the directional-control sizing analysis. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust generation
fha.effAc: No thrust available from any source; aircraft cannot sustain flight and continued controlled flight to a runway is not assured — forced descent/off-field outcome.
fha.effCrew: Crew faced with a total-thrust-loss emergency; glide/forced-landing management with no propulsive recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of all propulsive thrust removes the ability to sustain flight; effects support Catastrophic (loss of the aircraft). Proposed for confirmation; maps to Extremely Improbable / 1e-9 per fh objective. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous surface response to crew pitch/roll/yaw command
fha.effAc: Control surface moves other than as commanded, producing an unintended trajectory response; potential departure from intended flight path if not countered.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the mismatch between command and response and counter/annunciate; degraded-law reversion may follow.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The AFHA function definition (position primary/secondary flight control surfaces) does not by itself fix the magnitude/authority of the erroneous response or its phase-dependent recoverability; the aircraft effect (recoverable upset vs loss of control) cannot be bounded from the provided function alone. Severity left blank pending the erroneous-response magnitude and the flight-control voting/protection behaviour.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded surface motion with no crew command
fha.effAc: A surface moves with no crew input (e.g. hardover or runaway), producing an uncommanded trajectory excursion; recoverability depends on surface, authority and phase.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded motion and take corrective action; may require law reversion or opposing input.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify from the function definition alone: the aircraft effect ranges from a nuisance transient to loss of control depending on the affected surface, its authority and whether it is a hardover vs slow drift. The provided function does not bound the authority or rate of the uncommanded motion. Severity left blank pending that scope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift (flap/slat) extension
fha.effAc: Left/right high-lift mismatch produces a rolling moment and asymmetric lift during a low-speed, low-altitude configuration change; asymmetry brakes are provided at each section to arrest the runaway, but a residual asymmetry imposes a roll/handling demand.
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the roll, manage the configuration and fly a degraded approach/landing; workload elevated in a critical phase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The magnitude of retained asymmetry after the asymmetry brakes engage, and therefore the controllability outcome, is not stated by the AFHA function or the SDD; effect could range from a manageable handling penalty to a hazardous roll upset near the ground. Severity left blank pending the asymmetry-brake performance and the residual-asymmetry handling case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded flight-control surface drift below the crew detection threshold (malfunction), the surface departing commanded position gradually without annunciation
fha.effAc: Trajectory departs commanded state progressively; trim/authority is consumed to hold path; if undetected the divergence continues toward an out-of-trim or upset condition, worst at low-speed/high-workload phases
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no corrective action while below detection threshold; increasing control input eventually required with no clear cue as to cause
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: an undetected drift that consumes control authority and can progress to an out-of-trim/upset with no crew cue supports at least a large reduction in safety margins / significant crew workload (Hazardous). Whether it reaches Catastrophic depends on the true rate of divergence, phase, and recoverable authority remaining — not stated in the SDD; confirm against the drift rate and detection coverage. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight-control surface response to crew or autopilot command (malfunction), the surface moving incorrectly with no annunciation
fha.effAc: Aircraft responds contrary to or disproportionately to command; with no annunciation the crew cannot diagnose the source; potential for uncommanded trajectory excursion or upset, most severe at low altitude / high-workload phases
fha.effCrew: Crew act on a false picture (command believed honoured); corrective inputs may aggravate the response; no cue to the true surface state
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: an erroneous surface response that is undetected removes the crew's ability to diagnose or compensate and can produce an uncommanded upset at low altitude; that combination is consistent with a Catastrophic failure condition. Confirm the true undetectability against the FCS monitoring architecture (three dissimilar computers, asymmetry/jam discretes) — if the erroneous response is in fact annunciated this is a different, less severe condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected flight-control surface asymmetry (malfunction), left/right surfaces at differing positions without annunciation
fha.effAc: Rolling/yawing moment developed and held; without annunciation the crew trim against it without knowing the cause; asymmetry can grow toward a controllability limit, most critical at low speed and in the engine-out/blade-loaded directional-control case
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties, trimming out an unexplained asymmetry; no cue to the true surface disagreement
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: an undetected asymmetry that develops a sustained moment and consumes directional/lateral authority supports a large reduction in safety margins with significant workload (Hazardous). Escalation toward Catastrophic depends on the achievable asymmetry magnitude versus available authority in the directional sizing case — the SDD states the sizing case but not the surface-drift-driven asymmetry bound; confirm before finalising. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight-control authority within manoeuvre limits, control still available at reduced capability or increased difficulty but within the manoeuvre envelope
fha.effAc: Reduced control authority / rate; the aircraft remains controllable within the manoeuvre envelope; margins to limiting cases (engine-out directional case, gust/manoeuvre response) are reduced
fha.effCrew: Crew retain control with degraded handling; increased workload and reduced margin, condition annunciated (degraded-law annunciation available)
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: reduced authority that remains inside the manoeuvre envelope with annunciated degraded handling supports a significant reduction in safety margins / increase in crew workload (Major). Confirm against how much authority is lost and whether the residual still covers the engine-out directional sizing case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight-control authority outside manoeuvre limits, remaining authority insufficient to cover a required limiting manoeuvre or the sizing directional-control case
fha.effAc: Residual authority no longer covers a required limiting case (e.g. outboard engine failure at V1 with maximum blade payload); loss of controllability in that case, most critical at low speed / low altitude
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to command the required manoeuvre in the limiting case despite full input; recovery not assured
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED: authority falling below the manoeuvre envelope in the sizing directional-control case (engine-out at V1, blade payload) implies loss of controllability at low altitude, consistent with Catastrophic. Confirm which limiting case is breached and at what phase — the SDD names the sizing case but does not quantify the residual authority at which controllability is lost. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced directional control authority; degraded ability to counter asymmetric thrust or crosswind, with the outboard engine-out at max blade payload being the sizing case for rudder authority. Aircraft controllable but with reduced margin.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain directional control; degraded-law/asymmetry annunciation; possible need to reduce asymmetry or divert.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. The directional case (outboard engine-out at 28 m moment arm with max blade payload) is the sizing case for rudder authority per the SDD; a partial loss narrows an already sizing-critical margin. Confirm the assumed residual authority — partial degrees span a range and the classification depends on how much authority remains against the sizing case. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority; degraded ability to control flight path in pitch. Elevators are on hydraulic systems A and C with a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim, so a survivable degraded pitch means remains.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload; degraded-law annunciation; possible flare/manoeuvre limitation.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — CANNOT CLASSIFY from what is provided. The SDD gives elevators on A+C with mechanical reversion to stabiliser trim, but the aircraft-level effect of a PARTIAL pitch authority loss (how much authority remains, and whether it constrains flare/recovery in the landing case) is not stated. The severity turns on the residual pitch envelope, which the function definition does not support asserting. Confirm residual authority before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of roll control authority
fha.effAc: Reduced roll control authority; degraded ability to counter roll disturbances and crosswind at touchdown. Ailerons are on hydraulic systems B and C plus multi-function spoilers, so roll capability is degraded rather than lost.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain wings-level and lateral path; degraded-law annunciation.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — CANNOT CLASSIFY from what is provided. The SDD gives ailerons on B+C with multi-function spoilers, but the aircraft-level effect of a PARTIAL roll authority loss (residual roll rate/authority and its adequacy for the crosswind and landing cases) is not stated. Severity depends on residual authority not supported by the function definition. Confirm residual authority before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight-path control authority
fha.effAc: Complete loss of the ability to control the aircraft trajectory. The SDD provides a mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment as a survivable-but-degraded means with all FCCs lost; complete loss of flight-path control authority is the condition beyond any such means, leaving no means to control the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: No means to control the flight path; loss of the aircraft.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew loss.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Complete loss of the ability to control aircraft trajectory prevents continued safe flight and landing with no residual control means, consistent with Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). Note the SDD provides a mechanical reversion backstop; this TL condition is defined as loss beyond that backstop. Confirm the condition boundary against the reversion path. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking producing uncommanded ground path deviation
fha.effAc: Uncommanded lateral deviation of the ground path during braking; potential for runway excursion on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a predicted rollout of approximately 1,080 m. Anti-skid operates per wheel pair and steering is available to counter.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to correct the deviation via steering/differential braking; risk of loss of directional control on the ground if uncorrected.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — CANNOT CLASSIFY from what is provided. The severity of a ground-path deviation depends on the lateral excursion consequence — runway/overrun width and margin, and whether the deviation is correctable by nose-wheel steering within the strip — none of which are stated at aircraft level. The SDD gives the rollout/landing-distance longitudinal margin but not the lateral excursion consequence needed to derive severity. Confirm the excursion consequence before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded ground steering deflection (malfunction — nose-wheel steering deflects without or against crew command)
fha.effAc: Uncommanded nose-wheel deflection produces an unintended ground path; on the semi-prepared strip with ~720 m margin between the 1,800 m requirement and ~1,080 m rollout, a lateral excursion could depart the prepared surface. Magnitude of achievable deflection and available rudder/differential-braking counter is not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect and counter the deflection with tiller/pedal and differential braking; workload and time to react not characterised.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states steering is hydraulic from tiller/pedals with a mechanical tow disconnect but does not bound the deflection authority, the speed at which it can occur, or the counter-authority available, so the aircraft effect (recoverable path deviation vs. runway/strip excursion) cannot be established. Needs directional-control analysis and the excursion case on the semi-prepared surface.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to crew command (malfunction — braking output does not match commanded deceleration, including asymmetric or spurious application)
fha.effAc: Erroneous/asymmetric braking degrades or misdirects deceleration on a strip sized with only ~720 m margin (1,800 m required vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout); asymmetric application also induces an unintended ground path. Spurious application at speed could produce a directional upset or tyre/brake damage.
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the mismatch and counter with pedal modulation and steering; electrically signalled brake control means the error may not be intuitively attributable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD establishes the tight landing-distance margin and asymmetric-braking potential but does not quantify the deceleration error magnitude, the resulting stopping-distance shortfall on the semi-prepared surface, or the directional excursion, so the bounding aircraft effect is unestablished. Needs braking-performance and directional analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of braking capability (still braking but at reduced capability, e.g. loss of one hydraulic brake supply or reduced number of braked wheels)
fha.effAc: Reduced deceleration extends stopping distance. The system carries dual hydraulic brake supply plus accumulator reserve sized for six full applications, so a single-source loss leaves an alternate; against the ~720 m margin on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip a partial loss erodes but does not necessarily exhaust the margin. On a degraded/contaminated surface the residual margin is not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew applies alternate/accumulator braking per procedure; increased attention and possibly a longer rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects derived: extended stopping distance eroding the ~720 m landing margin with degraded surface performance not quantified, but redundant supply and accumulator reserve preserve a braking means — a significant reduction in safety margin / increase in crew workload rather than loss of the function. Confirm against contaminated-surface and RTO stopping analysis; worst case could rise if the semi-prepared margin is shown to be exhausted. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground directional steering (steering still available but at reduced authority or one channel lost)
fha.effAc: Reduced steering authority degrades directional control on the ground; differential braking and rudder remain available as alternate directional means. On the semi-prepared strip with narrow lateral margin, reduced authority increases the risk of path deviation in crosswind or on a soft surface. Residual authority and alternate effectiveness not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew supplements with differential braking and rudder; increased workload to hold centreline, especially in crosswind or on soft ground.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effects derived: degraded but not lost directional control with differential braking and rudder as alternates — a significant reduction in safety margin and increased crew workload rather than a controllability loss. Confirm; could be higher if analysis shows the semi-prepared/crosswind case cannot be held with the alternate means. Steering authority and alternate effectiveness are not quantified in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid protection (braking available but wheel-pair anti-skid function inoperative)
fha.effAc: Without anti-skid, braking on the semi-prepared / potentially low-friction surface risks wheel lock, skidding and directional instability, and reduced braking effectiveness that lengthens stopping distance against the ~720 m margin. Anti-skid operates per wheel pair, so loss may be per-pair or full; extent and stopping-distance penalty on the design surface are not quantified in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew must modulate braking manually to avoid lock-up; higher workload and skill demand, particularly on a low-friction strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states anti-skid operates per wheel pair but gives no braking penalty, minimum-friction assumption, or contaminated-surface stopping performance, so the aircraft effect (recoverable longer rollout vs. skid/excursion on the semi-prepared surface) cannot be bounded. Needs braking-performance analysis on the design surface with anti-skid inoperative.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking and ground steering
fha.effAc: No wheel deceleration or steering available on the ground; on the sizing landing case (predicted rollout ~1,080 m against an 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement) the deceleration margin is lost and a runway overrun / departure from the prepared surface is credible; reverse thrust on the two inboard engines and the accumulator-supported emergency braking (sized to six full applications) may partially arrest the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Crew loses primary means to decelerate and steer; must revert to reverse thrust and accumulator braking with limited applications; high workload directional-control task on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects point toward an overrun hazard on the sizing surface, but the SDD gives reverse thrust and accumulator braking (six applications, all three hydraulic systems lost) as reconfiguration paths whose adequacy against the 1,080 m / 1,800 m margin is not quantified. Cannot derive Catastrophic vs Hazardous without the residual-deceleration analysis; severity left empty pending that data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous restraint status indication showing secure when restraint is degraded
fha.effAc: Crew receives a false 'secure' indication while restraint of the single 72.6 t blade is actually degraded; aircraft may be dispatched or flight continued with an undetected restraint deficiency, permitting a load shift / CG excursion whose bounding structural and controllability effect is not stated in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Crew acts on false-secure information and takes no corrective or diversion action; no in-flight restraint adjustment is available.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The malfunction removes crew awareness of a degrading single-item 72.6 t restraint, but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level consequence of a load shift (CG-excursion limits, structural load-path capacity). Cannot classify without that bounding effect; severity left empty.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of payload restraint at one station
fha.effAc: Loss of restraint at a single station; per the design the load path is sized so the loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours, so blade restraint is maintained at reduced margin; loss of tension at one strap is annunciated and loss on two adjacent stations is annunciated as a condition requiring immediate attention.
fha.effCrew: Crew is annunciated of the reduced restraint and can assess; no in-flight restraint adjustment is available, so response is monitoring and diversion planning.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants beyond flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Design states the single-strap loss is carried by neighbours and is annunciated, which points to a reduced-margin condition rather than immediate load release; however the SDD does not quantify the residual restraint margin at one station lost, so the aircraft-level severity cannot be derived. Left empty pending restraint load-path substantiation.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of payload restraint — the single 72.6 t blade is unrestrained along the full 108 m hold length
fha.effAc: Loss of restraint on a single 72.6 t unitised blade permits longitudinal blade migration, producing large uncommanded shifts in centre of gravity and structural loading of the hold hard points; potential loss of controllability and structural failure of the load path.
fha.effCrew: Crew unable to arrest or re-restrain the blade in flight (no in-flight adjustment of restraint); flight becomes uncontrollable as CG departs limits.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect, but loss of aircraft is the credible outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncontrolled migration of a 72.6 t blade drives CG outside limits and overloads the hold hard points with no crew recovery means, a condition consistent with loss of the aircraft. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint tension undetected by the monitoring loop — restraint degraded with no crew indication
fha.effAc: Undetected loss of strap tension degrades the restraint margin on the blade; with the single instrumented tension loop failed the degradation is not annunciated, so progression toward blade migration proceeds without warning.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action; they receive no indication that restraint has degraded.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect depends on how much restraint capability is lost before detection is expected and whether neighbouring straps carry the load (SDD states one-strap loss is carried by neighbours); the extent of undetected degradation and its controllability consequence is not defined in the provided material, so the severity cannot be derived from the stated effects.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of the pressure interlock permitting an unlock command with residual differential present
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The pressure interlock is a safeguard on the ground unlock command and the SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight and is operated only from a ground handling panel. The provided material does not establish an in-flight aircraft effect for loss of the interlock alone (no stated path by which the door unlocks in flight), so no aircraft-level effect can be grounded and no severity derived without knowing whether an inadvertent in-flight unlock path exists.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous lock-closed indication with the visor not secured — no dissimilar disclosure to the crew
fha.effAc: The nose visor is a pressure-boundary and forward-fuselage structural load-path element; an undetected erroneous lock-closed indication permits dispatch and takeoff with the door unsecured and no disclosure, giving in-flight loss of the pressure boundary and forward structural load path.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties and take no action; both the displayed status and (in this unaware case) any disclosure means fail to reveal the door is not secured, so the take-off configuration check does not catch it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect, but loss of the pressure boundary / structural load path is a loss-of-aircraft path.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With no disclosure to the crew, an unsecured nose visor that is a pressure boundary and single structural load path opening in flight is consistent with loss of the aircraft. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of nose door lock engagement (subset of the twelve latches / eight pins not fully engaged) with the door forming the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path
fha.effAc: Reduced margin in the forward pressure boundary and structural load path; potential for lock disengagement under load. The aircraft-level consequence (loss of pressure boundary integrity / structural failure at the nose) depends on residual lock capacity vs. pressurisation and flight loads, which is not stated in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times and is in the take-off configuration check; crew can detect a not-fully-locked condition before dispatch.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD gives the door as pressure boundary and single structural load path (§5.7.1) but does not state the aircraft-level outcome of a PARTIAL lock loss under pressurisation/flight loads. Requires structural and pressurisation analysis to establish whether residual engagement holds the boundary; leave EMPTY pending that analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of one of the two dissimilar, independently routed nose-door lock-sensing paths (proximity sensing harness OR mechanical indicator linkage), with the second sensing path remaining available
fha.effAc: No change to actual door lock state; the door remains as locked. Loss of monitoring redundancy only — the surviving dissimilar path continues to report lock status.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains lock indication via the remaining sensing path; the loss of one channel reduces monitoring redundancy but not the lock confirmation itself.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is loss of one monitoring channel with a dissimilar independent channel still confirming lock (§5.7.2, §5.7.5); this points toward the benign end, but classifying it (Minor vs No Safety Effect) depends on whether latent single-path loss defeats detection of a later lock failure — a latency/exposure judgement not grounded in the SDD. Left EMPTY rather than reaching for Minor/No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of nose door lock confirmation (both sensing paths fail to confirm lock, or lock confirmation cannot be established) — the crew cannot verify the door forming the pressure boundary and forward-fuselage load path is locked
fha.effAc: Actual door state may be locked or unlocked; the aircraft-level consequence of dispatching or continuing with an unconfirmed/unlocked nose door (pressure boundary loss, structural load-path loss) is not established in the SDD.
fha.effCrew: Both flight-deck lock indications lost; crew cannot complete the take-off configuration lock check and cannot confirm the door state.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: door is pressure boundary and single structural load path (§5.7.1), and the door cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.6), but the SDD does not state the aircraft-level outcome of loss of lock confirmation. The severity turns on the worst credible actual door state and its pressurisation/structural consequence, which needs structural and pressurisation analysis; leave EMPTY.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pressurisation response to crew command — the pressurisation control drives fuselage differential to a state other than commanded
fha.effAc: Fuselage differential driven away from the commanded/scheduled value; the hold is sized to a low differential only. The aircraft-level consequence depends on whether the error can exceed structural relief limits or produce an unacceptable cabin/hold altitude, bounded by independent positive/negative relief valves (§5.9.2).
fha.effCrew: Differential pressure and cabin altitude are displayed to the crew and to the crew oxygen logic; crew can select the manual pressurisation mode. Crew oxygen is available for a loss-of-pressure event.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only. Crew oxygen sized for the diversion at maximum operating altitude.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: independent mechanical relief protects the structure regardless of control (§5.9.2), and the hold is unoccupied with crew oxygen available, which bounds the outcome — but the SDD does not state the achievable erroneous differential vs. structural limits or resulting cabin altitude. Severity requires the pressurisation schedule and structural relief analysis; leave EMPTY.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded change in fuselage pressure differential without crew command — pressurisation drifts or steps away from the scheduled differential absent any command
fha.effAc: Differential departs the schedule without command; bounded by two independent controllers, two outflow valves (either sufficient), a pneumatic backup, and independent positive/negative relief (§5.9.2, §5.9.3). The aircraft-level outcome (rate/magnitude of uncommanded change vs. limits) is not stated.
fha.effCrew: Differential and cabin altitude displayed; crew alerted and can revert to manual/pneumatic backup mode; crew oxygen available.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold in flight; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: extensive control/relief redundancy (§5.9.3) bounds the outcome and crew have indication plus manual reversion, but the SDD does not state the achievable uncommanded differential or its cabin-altitude/structural effect. Do not default to a benign class; severity needs pressurisation and structural analysis. Left EMPTY.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded drift in pressure differential below the detection threshold, crew unaware
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight, no occupant effect from the hold volume
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state the direction (over- or under-pressure) or the magnitude the undetected drift can reach, so the effect on cabin altitude at the flight-deck / on structure relative to the mechanical relief setting cannot be bounded. Need drift limit vs relief-valve setting and vs crew-tolerable flight-deck cabin altitude to derive a severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Degraded pressure control remaining within the pressurisation schedule limits
fha.effAc: Pressure differential maintained within schedule; single-pack / single-controller / single-outflow-valve operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule
fha.effCrew: Reconfiguration is automatic; crew workload minimal, condition annunciated
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight, no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Minor: control is retained within schedule limits with reduced redundancy (two controllers, two outflow valves, either sufficient; single-pack permitted). Effect is a slight reduction in safety margins / slight increase in crew workload, not an operational limitation approaching structural or physiological limits. Confirm against the tolerable cabin-altitude schedule. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Pressure control degraded outside the pressurisation schedule limits
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight, no occupant effect from the hold volume
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: 'outside schedule limits' is not quantified in the SDD. Without the bound on how far cabin altitude/differential can deviate and its relation to the flight-deck physiological limits and structural relief settings, the effect on aircraft and crew cannot be stated and no severity can be derived. Need the schedule-limit values and the excursion envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fuselage pressure differential control
fha.effAc: Loss of controlled differential; positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system, bounding the structural over/under-pressure case; flight-deck cabin altitude follows aircraft altitude toward ambient
fha.effCrew: Flight crew don quick-donning oxygen masks (crew oxygen system sized for four occupants for the diversion time at max operating altitude), initiate descent and diversion; maximum operating altitude is FL260
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight, no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effects are grounded but a severity is not yet derivable: it hinges on the achievable flight-deck cabin altitude if control is lost at FL260 and on time-of-useful-consciousness versus mask-donning time. Crew oxygen availability and the FL260 ceiling point toward Major rather than Hazardous, but the tolerable cabin-altitude and the emergency-descent capability need to be confirmed before classifying — left empty rather than assumed.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ice protection activation without an accretion condition present
fha.effAc: Bleed demand to the environmental system reduces pack capacity when in use; the wing-anti-ice performance penalty is applied automatically to displayed performance; no accretion is actually present
fha.effCrew: Condition annunciated (zone health/status to avionics); crew has manual on/off selection; slight increase in awareness/workload
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight, no occupant effect
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Minor: erroneous activation consumes bleed and imposes a performance penalty that is automatically reflected in displayed performance, giving at most a slight reduction in capability and a slight increase in crew workload; the crew retains manual control. Confirm the performance/bleed margin at the limiting condition supports Minor rather than Major. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to activate ice protection when accretion is present (crew aware via ice detection advisory)
fha.effAc: Ice accretes on unprotected/should-be-protected surfaces, inlets and probes; increased drag, reduced lift/control-surface effectiveness and possible engine-inlet/probe degradation until protection is restored or icing is exited.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by ice detection advisory and by failure-to-activate annunciation; assumed to select manual activation and/or exit the icing envelope by altitude/route change.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction (accretion with drag/lift/probe degradation) is grounded, but the SDD gives no quantified aerodynamic or handling penalty of accretion on this airframe, and manual activation plus icing-exit is available to an aware crew. Severity cannot be derived without the icing-envelope handling/performance substantiation; leaving empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Failure to activate ice protection when accretion is present with ice detection unavailable (crew unaware of accretion)
fha.effAc: Ice accretes progressively on protected surfaces, inlets and probes with no detection cue; drag rises and lift/control-surface effectiveness degrades, with possible probe/engine-inlet effects, continuing unchecked while the crew fly normally.
fha.effCrew: Detection advisory unavailable; crew continue duties, take no icing action, and receive no cue to activate protection or exit the icing envelope.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Unaware, unchecked accretion is more severe than the aware case, but the magnitude depends on the aerodynamic/handling penalty of accretion on this airframe, which the SDD does not quantify. Severity cannot be derived from the provided material; leaving empty per abstention rather than reaching for a value.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of ice protection on a subset of protected surfaces (partial loss; crew aware)
fha.effAc: Protection lost on one or more zones (e.g. a stabiliser heater zone, a wing/cowl bleed subset, or a heated probe) while other zones remain protected; localised accretion possible on the affected surface until icing is exited.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone is annunciated; crew assumed to restrict operation in icing and/or exit the icing envelope for the affected zone.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Which subset is lost and its aerodynamic/probe consequence is not resolvable from the function definition, and the accretion penalty per zone is not quantified in the SDD. Effects stated but severity cannot be derived; leaving empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of ice detection with ice protection retained (crew aware of detection loss)
fha.effAc: Protection remains fully available; only the automatic detection/advisory function is lost. No accretion occurs if protection is selected on; risk is that automatic activation no longer triggers on accretion.
fha.effCrew: Loss of detection annunciated; crew assumed to select manual/continuous ice protection so that protection no longer depends on the lost detector.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Protection is retained and can be selected on manually, so the aircraft effect is limited; but whether continued icing operation is permitted with detection lost, and the workload/procedure basis, are not in the provided material. Severity not derivable; leaving empty per abstention rather than choosing the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of protection on a heated zone or probe (partial loss; crew unaware)
fha.effAc: Protection is lost on a zone or probe without annunciation; accretion develops locally with no crew cue — potential for erroneous probe data (airspeed/AoA/altitude) or localised surface accretion progressing unchecked.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of the lost zone; crew continue normally, take no action, and — for a heated probe — may act on erroneous air-data without recognising its cause.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Undetected loss of a heated probe (erroneous, unflagged air-data) could be significantly more severe than an undetected wing/stab zone; the function definition does not distinguish which and the SDD does not quantify the consequence. Severity cannot be derived without that resolution and the air-data effect substantiation; leaving empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice protection capability
fha.effAc: With no protection to wings, cowls, stabiliser zones, probes and detectors, ice accretion in the icing envelope degrades lift/drag and control margins and can corrupt air-data sensing; the aircraft cannot safely continue in icing conditions.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to loss of protection and to detection advisory; assumed to exit icing conditions by altitude/route change and divert. Workload increased.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect (accretion degrading lift/drag, control and air-data) is stated, but the SDD does not fix the icing envelope of the certification basis, the exposure to that envelope on the point-to-point profile, or whether an escape manoeuvre is always available; without the encounter/escape basis the effects do not deterministically drive Hazardous vs Major. Severity left blank pending the icing certification basis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or misleading information presented on displays (crew aware)
fha.effAc: Misleading primary information (attitude, air data, engine, configuration) could drive an inappropriate crew response; because the crew becomes aware through inconsistency with the independent standby instrument and cross-checks, they revert to trusted sources and the aircraft trajectory is recovered.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the discrepancy against the independent standby attitude/airspeed/altitude and other displays, identify the misleading source, and revert. Increased workload during identification.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Major: misleading information is potentially hazardous, but the SDD provides an independent standby instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries, so an aware crew can cross-check and revert, bounding the aircraft effect. Engineer to confirm against the specific misleading-parameter set. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous, missing or mis-prioritised crew alert (crew aware)
fha.effAc: A wrong, absent or mis-prioritised alert delays or misdirects the crew's response to an underlying failure; with the crew aware of the alerting anomaly (e.g. inconsistency between alert and displayed system state) they interrogate system status directly and apply the correct procedure, limiting the aircraft effect.
fha.effCrew: Crew notice the alert does not match displayed system state, consult system pages/procedures directly, and act. Increased workload and potential for a delayed response.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Aircraft effect depends on which underlying failure the mis-alert masks or misdirects — the alerting system consolidates every system's status, so the severity is inherited from the worst underlying condition whose annunciation is corrupted. The SDD does not scope that set at aircraft level, so the effects do not fix a single class. Severity left blank pending the alert-coverage set.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected missing or suppressed crew alert (crew unaware)
fha.effAc: An underlying failure occurs but its alert is missing or suppressed with no indication to the crew; the crew do not act on the failure and it progresses unmitigated, so the aircraft effect is the unannunciated worst-case outcome of whatever condition should have been alerted.
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware of the underlying failure; continue normal duties and take no action. No cue.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The aircraft effect is inherited from the worst underlying failure whose alert is suppressed, defeated by the loss of annunciation; the alerting system covers every system's status but the SDD does not enumerate that set at aircraft level, so the effects do not fix a single class. Severity left blank pending the suppressed-alert coverage set. Do not default to the benign end.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of a subset of flight-crew displays or alerting channels, remainder retained
fha.effAc: A subset of display or alerting channels is unavailable; core information and alerting remain presentable on the retained channels, including reversionary display selection to any surviving display unit.
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to reconfigure and cross-check on the remaining channels; primary flight, navigation and alerting information remains available.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect is a partial loss with the remaining channels retaining primary information and alerting; whether the residual workload and reduced margin reaches Minor or Major depends on which subset is lost and the redundancy actually credited (three display processors, dual networks, independent standby instrument) — not derivable at aircraft-function level from the definition alone. Left empty for engineer to classify against the credited architecture.. Engineer to classify.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight-crew displays and consolidated alerting
fha.effAc: No flight, navigation or system information is presented on the primary displays and no consolidated alerting is available; the crew's only remaining information is the independent standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude), which shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries.
fha.effCrew: Crew lose all primary displays and all consolidated alerting simultaneously; flight must be continued on the standby instrument alone with no system-status or alerting information, a severe increase in workload and loss of situational awareness in which subsequent failures go entirely unannunciated.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight, flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Displays and consolidated alerting are the crew's sole integrated means to fly, navigate and manage every other aircraft system; their complete loss leaves only a standby instrument with no alerting, and in IMC/low flight levels this reduces safety margins and crew capability such that the effects support Catastrophic. PROPOSED for confirmation — final class depends on the credited independence of the standby instrument and the residual capability it provides. — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: The eight parent aircraft-function statements are a safety-team derivation, not text stated in the SDD.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly declines to enumerate aircraft-level functions, so parent statements had to be derived from per-system purpose text.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a derived parent function is mis-framed, its sub-function allocation and any downstream AFHA failure condition rolling up to it change.

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.text: FUE, HYD, EPS and EWS are resources, not aircraft functions, and are therefore excluded from the function list.
assumptions.rationale: The modeling rule and the SDD both classify these as resources supplying other systems rather than behaviours the aircraft accomplishes.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any of these must appear as a function, the decomposition gains additional parent functions and the Resources model shifts.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS from the emitted functions.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft themselves

assumptions.text: The nose door structure and hold floor hard points are structure, not functional-FHA items, so only the lock/monitor behaviours are authored as functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door is a single load path treated as structure; structural integrity is substantiated by structural analysis and PRA, not the functional FHA.
assumptions.ifWrong: If structural load-path integrity is captured as a function, an additional (incorrect) functional-FHA item would be created.
assumptions.usedFor: Nose door and cargo restraint sub-functions (lock/monitor only).

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: SF-001 'control thrust magnitude and direction' at aircraft level is interpreted as covering both total/partial thrust loss and thrust-asymmetry (directional) malfunctions, not a thrust-vectoring capability.
assumptions.rationale: The function name says 'direction' but the SDD describes fixed podded turbofans with no thrust vectoring; 'direction' must therefore mean the asymmetry/yawing-moment aspect.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a distinct thrust-direction capability exists, SF-001 needs additional total/partial-loss conditions for that capability.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 malfunction 'asymmetric thrust producing uncommanded yawing moment' and partial 'controllable asymmetry'.

citations.quote: Four podded turbofans on pylons beneath the high wing provide thrust for all phases of flight

assumptions.text: Erroneous/uncommanded control-surface and thrust behaviour can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying the crew-Unaware rows.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD documents no detection means with a stated threshold for slow drift or gradual asymmetry, so an undetectable variant cannot be dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If intrinsic cues always alert the crew, the Unaware rows for SF-001/SF-002/SF-005 collapse into the Aware rows.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001 Unaware, SF-002 Unaware, SF-005 Unaware rows.

assumptions.text: The restraint tension monitoring loop has a coverage gap such that some loss of strap tension is undetectable in flight, supporting the SF-004 Unaware partial.
